objective: Coordinator's go-ahead (19 November 2026) on MEET-ONCE-20261119-001's direction 1. UNIQUE-TABLE-20261119-001's six static pairs meet once and have other states with the same bond-distance table, but the law never reaches them; MEET-ONCE found no reached meet-once collision with other states up to 40 junctions. Find a property that every reached stage has and the static rivals lack, prove that complete rounds preserve it, and test whether it (with meeting once) is enough for the table to carry the allowed states, which with the proof would give the statement at every size. Serves A97 and G1.
status: Complete 2026-11-19 (Partial; referee pending; census last shard pending): the law never builds UNIQUE-TABLE's rivals at any size, because complete rounds keep backed pairs (any two junctions met by a junction with a loose distinction also meet an older, closed junction), which every rival lacks (proved; 70,228 census stages checked). But backed pairs do not keep the states: among 503,039 legal meet-once arrangements of at most 7 junctions, 242 other-states pairs have both sides backed, so MEET-ONCE's result does not follow at every size from this property; pairs peeling twice or regrown by the law were too few to test.
stop_rule: A property splitting reached stages from the rivals, its preservation proved or refuted, and the static test of sufficiency at up to 7 junctions; referee hand-off; report.
title: Why does the growth never reach the static pairs?
